title: ¡Así se dice! Spanish 1 (Level 1)

sources.what: teacher course site (McGraw Hill online text): Spanish I chapter list, Capítulos 1-9 with titles
Spanish 1 review site: Capítulos 1-4 titles and the preliminary-unit grammar review list

district Spanish 1 curriculum built on "McGraw Hill - Glencoe Spanish Asi se dice! Level 1": nine units with vocabulary themes and grammar objectives (units map to the preliminary lessons and Chapters 1-7 by theme)
Bridgeton (NJ) Spanish II pacing chart: Level 1 Chapters 7-11 with themes, grammar and Student Edition page ranges
McGraw Hill program page: Level 1 has 11 thematic chapters; Chapters 10 and 11 are repeated in Level 2
Bookshare record confirming ISBN 9780021367474 = ¡Así se dice! Spanish 1, Conrad J. Schmitt, McGraw-Hill Education, 2016

summary: Glencoe/McGraw Hill's first-year Spanish textbook: preliminary lessons and eleven thematic chapters, each with Vocabulario, Gramática, Conversación and Lectura cultural sections and a chapter review (section names general). Grammar runs from ser, tener and present-tense regular verbs through stem-changing verbs, ser versus estar and object pronouns to the preterite, the present progressive and reflexive verbs.

toc.label: Lecciones preliminares
toc.covers: Opening lessons before Chapter 1: greetings and farewells, courtesy expressions, numbers 0-100, telling time, days and months, seasons and weather.

toc.label: Capítulo 1
toc.title: ¿Cómo somos?
toc.covers: Describing people and classes: nationalities and descriptive adjectives with agreement, subject pronouns, the verb ser, de for origin, asking questions with ser.

toc.label: Capítulo 2
toc.title: La familia y la casa
toc.covers: Family members, pets and the home: the verb tener (including describing hair and eye color), possessive adjectives; the district plan also teaches estar for location and ser versus estar here.

toc.label: Capítulo 3
toc.title: En clase y después
toc.covers: School clothes and uniforms, school supplies, classroom and after-school activities, places in town: regular -ar verbs in the present and prepositional phrases of location.

toc.label: Capítulo 4
toc.title: ¿Qué comemos y dónde?
toc.covers: Foods and meals, ordering at a café, tipping, street food: regular -er and -ir verbs, tener que and deber, ir a + infinitive for future plans, acabar de.

toc.label: Capítulo 5
toc.title: Deportes
toc.covers: Team sports and games: stem-changing verbs (e>ie, o>ue) and verbs like gustar, interesar and aburrir with indirect object pronouns to state likes and dislikes.

toc.label: Capítulo 6
toc.title: El bienestar
toc.covers: Personality, feelings and health, a visit to the doctor: ser versus estar with adjectives, estar for feelings and location, indirect object pronouns.

toc.label: Capítulo 7
toc.title: De vacaciones
toc.covers: Summer beach and winter ski vacations, weather; preterite of regular -ar verbs, preterite of ir and ser, direct object pronouns lo, la, los, las; resorts in Spain and Argentina (Student Edition pp. 226-253 in the pacing chart).

toc.label: Capítulo 8
toc.title: En tu tiempo libre
toc.covers: Birthday parties, concerts and cultural events, movies and museums; preterite of -er and -ir verbs, oír and leer in the preterite, affirmative and negative words; Hispanic art and music (pp. 262-285).

toc.label: Capítulo 9
toc.title: ¡Vamos de compras!
toc.covers: Shopping for clothes and food at stores and markets; numbers above 100, saber versus conocer, comparatives and superlatives, demonstrative adjectives and pronouns (pp. 294-319).

toc.label: Capítulo 10
toc.title: En avión
toc.covers: Packing and air travel, at the airport and on the plane; present-tense verbs with -g- in the yo form (hacer, poner, traer, salir) and the present progressive; air travel in South America (pp. 328-356).

toc.label: Capítulo 11
toc.title: Una rutina diferente
toc.covers: Parts of the body, daily routine, backpacking and camping; reflexive verbs and commands, including asking a favor (pp. 362-387).

notes: None of the sources names its printing; ¡Así se dice! kept the same chapter sequence across its 2009-2016 national editions (general), so treat the outline as the same series rather than a verified 2016 match. Chapter 3 appears as "En clase y después" on one site and "En la escuela" on another. Grammar for the preliminary lessons and Chapters 1-6 comes from a district unit plan whose units follow the book's themes but are not numbered by chapter; Chapters 7-11 come from a pacing chart keyed to chapter numbers and pages. Chapters 10 and 11 open Level 2 again, so many schools save them for Spanish 2.
